chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Muhammad ibn Sowqat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever eats a morsel of fat, it expels the like of it from the ailments.

key_terms.لُقْمَة: a morsel or bite of food

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of eating fat on the body according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the consumption of animal fat (shahm) directly to the accumulation of disease, reflecting the Shia tradition of integrating physical health with spiritual purity. This hadith is often cited in fiqh and tafsir discussions to support the recommendation of limiting fatty foods, viewing them not merely as dietary choices but as factors that influence bodily humors and susceptibility to illness.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Sowqat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who eats a morsel of fat, throws out the likes of it from the ailments’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from Muhammad ibn Sawqah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one eats a morsel of shahm (fat) it expels the same amount of illness out.’”
